stage: builder self-score at phase 1 (written instruction + environment); the blind contract_review scores it again
pre_mortem: A strong solver reads the plan, writes its own statement model from sections 2-7, fuzzes the package against it and repairs split bookings, marginal bands, band rounding, the reversal window, the new-logo floor on small splits, draw recovery and the minimum payment; all seven departures are self-verifiable. Its own model has to give a value to the two lines the plan leaves unpriced (a credit note below 50,000 cents, a first order below 250,000 cents). If it reads each rule's defined subject as the rule's reach and keeps shipped code outside it, it keeps both (and fuzzing agrees with it); if it reads the shipped pricing of those items as the over-application of 5.1/6.1 (instinct: courtesy credits and trial orders earn or cost nothing), it zeroes them and its fuzz confirms that too. If it fixes 7.4 or 5.1 by editing the shared table entries in place, its own model (written from the plan) cannot see that the silent lines moved.
decisive_reason: Two exclusion-pull traps whose silent lines share an expression and a table figure with a departure; self-testing reproduces whatever reading the solver chose, but the same 'keep outside the subject' policy disarms both, so a 2/2 remains plausible (crop-hail went 2/2 twice on the shared-table shape; supplier-rebate split 1/2 only through the exclusion reading).
